system: Behavioral Health, Nervous Systems and Special Senses
outline: Disorders relating to the spine, spinal cord, and spinal nerve roots
primary_competency: Medical Knowledge: Applying Foundational Science Concepts
diagnosis: Syringomyelia with anterior white commissure involvement
mechanism: A central spinal-cord syrinx initially expands near the central canal and damages second-order pain-and-temperature fibers of the spinothalamic pathway as they decussate through the anterior white commissure. This produces bilateral segmental loss of pain and temperature, classically in a cape-like distribution when the cervical cord is involved, while dorsal-column modalities such as vibration and proprioception remain preserved early because those pathways lie farther posteriorly.
vignette: A 27-year-old woman reports repeatedly burning her shoulders and forearms without noticing the injury. Examination shows bilateral loss of pinprick and temperature sensation over the shoulders and upper arms. Light touch, vibration, and joint-position sense are preserved. Strength and deep tendon reflexes are normal. MRI of the cervical spinal cord shows a small fluid-filled cavity centered around the central canal.
lead: Which of the following neural structures is most directly responsible for the sensory deficit in this patient?
correct: Decussating spinothalamic fibers in the anterior white commissure
distractors: Ipsilateral dorsal columns of the cervical spinal cord
Dorsal root ganglion cell bodies supplying the upper extremities
Medial lemniscus fibers in the medulla
distractor_notes: The dorsal columns carry vibration, fine touch, and conscious proprioception in the spinal cord. These modalities are specifically preserved in this patient.

The lateral corticospinal tracts carry descending motor commands. Early selective injury to the anterior white commissure produces the dissociated sensory loss shown here without the upper motor neuron weakness expected from corticospinal involvement.

Dorsal root ganglia contain first-order sensory neuron cell bodies for multiple modalities. Bilateral selective loss of pain and temperature across several cervical dermatomes with preservation of dorsal-column modalities is better localized to the central crossing spinothalamic fibers.

The medial lemniscus carries dorsal-column modalities after those fibers decussate in the medulla. A lesion there would affect vibration, discriminative touch, and proprioception rather than selectively abolishing segmental pain and temperature.
key_expl: This patient's cervical syrinx produces classic dissociated sensory loss. Pain- and temperature-carrying second-order spinothalamic neurons cross the spinal cord through the anterior white commissure. A centrally expanding syrinx therefore interrupts these crossing fibers first, causing bilateral segmental loss of pain and temperature. The posterior columns remain relatively distant from the central cavity early in disease, explaining preservation of vibration and position sense.
objective: Localize the early sensory deficit of cervical syringomyelia to decussating spinothalamic fibers in the anterior white commissure, producing bilateral pain/temperature loss with preserved dorsal-column modalities.
